headline: Recce Pharmaceuticals secures Vietnam patent for anti-infective drug technology, extending IP protection to 2041 as Phase 3 trial in Indonesia nears completion
reasoning: Recce Pharmaceuticals has secured its eighth granted patent in Vietnam (family four), extending protection for its lead anti-infective compounds through 2041. The company has a late-stage Phase 3 trial running in Indonesia targeting diabetic foot ulcer infections, with approval expected by end of calendar year. Indonesian approval would provide data applicability across all ASEAN nations, including Vietnam. The company highlights a major unmet medical need given no new antibiotic class in over 40 years and ~75% penicillin resistance prevalence in the region. Recce also benefits from a government-guaranteed R&D rebate covering overseas expenditure up to ~$85 million over three years, providing non-dilutive funding security.
quote: This of our family, four of patients and we have 5 to 6 families of patients is our eight granted patents in family four alone and over 40 granted patents around that, taking our marketing and manufacturing monopolies out to 2041, in fact beyond. When we looked at the icon, we're really looking to the rise of diabetes across those countries. In fact, in Indonesia, where we have our late stage phase three diabetic foot ulcer infection study, the diabetes prevalence is 11%, rising to around 15% across the region. And if you have diabetes, 60% of those in their lifetime will get a diabetic ulcer and 80% of those will become infected. There is no standard of care.
